title: Syncing a 2D Phaser world canvas with a custom React desktop shell loop
author: arealguywithajob
selftext:
Long time lurker and first time posting here.

I wanted to share a look at an upcoming engine overhaul for my project, CodeGrind, which teaches programming and interview prep by translating data structures and algorithm problems into a live Tower Defense loop. I'll be dropping a ton of active gameplay clips soon, but I wanted to share this specific clip first because the engineering behind it was a massive puzzle and I’d love to get some feedback on the vibe.

The video shows the transition sequence I’ve been building. The game seamlessly shifts from a top-down 2D Phaser environment into a retro-themed desktop shell that serves as the main code workspace interface.

Architecturally, the overlay stack uses React, Chakra UI, and Framer Motion running directly alongside the Phaser canvas instance. The hardest part of the tech was mapping out a custom runtime bridge to handle state transfer and window focus between those separate engine layers without choking the performance loop.

This desktop environment acts as the sandbox where players interact with specialized LLM code-generation mechanics, building out and defending their solutions wave by wave. To win the level, you must solve the problem correctly and also survive the final wave.

This was originally built as a better way for me to prepare for interviews, but I think that there is a bigger use out there to teach people how to properly code with AI assistance.

Art and music was human created, code was AI generated and reviewed by me. I planned and designed every bit of this going back and forth with AI.

I'm pretty proud of how clean the handoff feels now, but let me know what you think of the CRT boot sequence or the interface transition! Always down to talk architecture if anyone has questions about bridging React and Phaser.
